requirements.txt pins the Python anthropic SDK only as >=0.20.0, with no upper bound. The source says SDKs older than the new majors keep sending 2023-06-01, so the new Python major presumably sends 2026-10-21 by default, and a fresh install or CI run would pull it. The call at ai_provider.py:135 passes temperature, which returns 400 in 2026-10-21, so every Anthropic generation request would fail. Uncertain: the changelog quoted is for TypeScript, so the migration agent should confirm which Python anthropic release defaults to 2026-10-21. Then choose one fix: add an upper bound (e.g. anthropic<1.0) for now, or upgrade deliberately and remove temperature from the Anthropic call. If any document blocks or citations are sent, also check them against the 2026-10-21 rules.
This task also resolves these changes. Handle each in the same change, and say in the PR how:
- anthropic:2026-10-21-sampling-params-removed (field-removed): In API version 2026-10-21, temperature, top_p and top_k in Messages and Batch requests return 400. The 400 on temperature/top_p/top_k only happens once requests carry anthropic-version 2026-10-21. The same edit fixes both: either pin the Python SDK below its new major, or move to 2026-10-21 and drop temperature from the messages.create call.
  Source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/migration-2026-10-21.md

record.prBody:
## New Claude API version 2026-10-21 (anthropic-version header); SDKs older than the new majors keep sending 2023-06-01 [Verified]

### Change

Removed temperature from the Anthropic messages.create call, made response reading robust (join text blocks instead of content[0].text), raised requirements to anthropic>=1.0.0 (2.4.0 installed in sandbox sends 2026-10-21). Added tests/test_anthropic_version.py (mocked transport) asserting version header 2026-10-21, no temperature/top_p/top_k in the body, and parsed text.

Files touched:
- `ai_provider.py`
- `requirements.txt`
- `tests/test_anthropic_version.py`

### Why

API version 2026-10-21 returns 400 when temperature/top_p/top_k is sent; the new SDK major sends that version by default.

> This guide lists the code changes for moving from API version `2023-06-01` to `2026-10-21`.

Source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/migration-2026-10-21.md

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| anthropic-proof | fail (1) | pass | 0 |

New failures: 0

Checks added by the agent (they count toward proof; check that each command really tests the change):
- anthropic-proof, added by the agent: `python -m pytest tests/test_anthropic_version.py -q` (fail (1) → pass)

Provider validators: none run.

Test of this change: `anthropic-proof`, written by the agent and run with the checks.

Where checks ran: Docker container python:3.12-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- No live API call
- Default model claude-3-sonnet-20240229 is deprecated/retired; model id not changed
- Test uses httpx2 (the transport the installed anthropic 2.x depends on); the exact SDK release where 2026-10-21 became default was not independently confirmed beyond the test passing on 2.4.0
- OpenAI/GitHub providers still send temperature (unaffected)
- No provider validator was run.

### Behaviour changes

- TEMPERATURE config no longer affects the Anthropic provider (still used by OpenAI and GitHub Models); Claude output sampling now uses API defaults
- Response text now concatenates all text blocks rather than only the first block

---

review.summary: The diff updates the only Anthropic call site (ai_provider.py:135). It bumps the SDK floor, drops `temperature` and makes text extraction tolerate non-text content blocks. The new test checks the outgoing `anthropic-version` header and the absence of sampling params through a mock transport. That is reasonable evidence for the request shape, but it never makes a live call. Several things are unconfirmed and should be checked against the migration guide and SDK: the `httpx2` import, whether `anthropic>=1.0.0` is really the major that sends 2026-10-21, and whether removing `temperature` is required or only a behaviour change. The configured model also needs to work under the new version. 'Verified' is defensible for the request shape but not for runtime behaviour.

concerns.issue: `temperature=config.temperature` was removed only from the Anthropic call; OpenAI and GitHub Models still honour it. If the 2026-10-21 guide does not actually reject or remove sampling params for the models used here, this silently changes output determinism for Anthropic users. I could not confirm the requirement from the single quoted line; check the migration guide's section on sampling parameters.

`anthropic>=1.0.0` assumes 1.0.0 is the first SDK major that sends `anthropic-version: 2026-10-21`. I could not confirm that version number. Check the SDK changelog or release notes. There is also no upper bound, so a later major could change behaviour again.

The test does `import httpx2 as httpx` and passes an `httpx2.Client` to `client.with_options(http_client=...)`. I don't recognise `httpx2`. It is not listed in requirements.txt, so it only works if the new SDK pulls it in transitively and accepts that client type. Confirm against the SDK's installed dependencies and the type of its `http_client` parameter. Otherwise the test will break on a clean install.

The default and configured model (docstring cites 'claude-3-sonnet-20240229'; config.anthropic_model is not shown) is never exercised against the real API. The mock returns model 'x'. If that model is retired or unsupported under 2026-10-21, every call fails. Because the error is caught, printed and returned as "", the app would silently fall back to rule-based descriptions with no visible failure.
The test mutates the global `ai_provider.config.anthropic_api_key` and never restores it. That can leak into other tests and change which provider `get_ai_provider` selects.

Joining all text blocks is a minor behaviour change from taking `content[0]`: multiple text blocks are now concatenated with no separator. It is harmless here, and safer if a non-text block comes first.

Confirm which anthropic SDK release first sends anthropic-version 2026-10-21, and that 1.0.0 is correct.
Verify `httpx2` is installed by the SDK and is the client type `with_options(http_client=...)` expects, or add it to requirements.txt.
Check config.anthropic_model's default and confirm that model works under API version 2026-10-21 with one live call.

## claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 retires on the Claude API Nov 30, 2026; use claude-sonnet-5-5 [Not affected]

### Change

No change made. The repo never names claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929. The Anthropic model comes from config.py:44, `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`, which defaults to `claude-3-sonnet-20240229`. A search for `4-5` and `20250929` across the repo found nothing.

No files changed.

### Why

The Nov 30, 2026 retirement covers only claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929, and this repo doesn't reference it. The code at ai_provider.py:135 passes the model from config. Its default is a different model, `claude-3-sonnet-20240229`.

> | November 30, 2026 | `claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929` | `claude-sonnet-5-5` |

Source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/model-deprecations.md

### Proof

No checks were run.

New failures: 0

Provider validators: none run.

Where checks ran: Docker container python:3.12-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- A deployed ANTHROPIC_MODEL env var could be set to claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929. The sandbox has no real env files, so I couldn't check.
- The default claude-3-sonnet-20240229 is a separate, already-retired model. I left it alone because it is out of scope for this task.
- No checks were run.

### Behaviour changes

None intended.
